conviction_note: A bottom-up build from the company's own Q3 guides (NIM ~2.75%, expenses just under $39M) plus a quarter of higher mortgage rates lands at about $0.84-0.87, against a $0.86-0.87 consensus. That is in line to a hair light. The quarter's 70-85bp rise in long yields cuts into AOCI/TBV and mortgage banking, while the Sept 16 Fed hike supports the Q4 NIM guide on the company's own repricing slide. None of it is a decisive unpriced number, so p_up sits at 47 on abs 4.5 (-0.27). Findings sum -0.5; the two measurements agree in sign and are both small.

findings.finding: A bottom-up Q3 build from the company's own guides gives EPS of about $0.84-0.87 and revenue of about $61-61.5M, against a $0.86-0.87 / $62.5M consensus. Inputs: Q2 NII $41.8M, plus the $0.7M final hedge-amortization benefit management already put in the 2.75% NIM guide, plus an extra day and ~2.5% commercial loan growth, gives ~$43.0-43.3M NII. Expenses just under $39M (guided). Fees ~$17.8-18.3M against Q2 $18.7M, because Q2 carried seasonal tax-servicing fees, wealth AUA (65% equity / 26% fixed income) was roughly flat in a quarter of S&P +2% and falling bonds, and mortgage banking ($3.5M in Q2) faced 30-year rates rising to 6.76% on 2026-09-10, the highest in over a year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS of $0.83 beat ~$0.77-0.79 and the stock rose +8.15%, though that print also showed credit stabilizing. Q1 2026 missed ($0.66 vs $0.77) on office-loan provisions and fell -16.9%. Plain NII/fee beats and misses without a credit story moved the stock 2-4% (Oct 2025 +2.65%, Jul 2025 -2.34%).
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus of $0.86-0.87 sits above a build that uses only the company's own guide. That suggests the estimates were set off the Q2 beat and the hedge tailwind and not marked down for a quarter of rising mortgage rates and the absence of Q2's seasonal fees. If the market had priced a light quarter, the -6% 20-day drift would be the only sign; it is partly that. But the drift coincides with a sector-wide rise in long yields, so it says nothing about this company's fee line.
findings.independence: Mortgage rate path: Freddie Mac PMMS 6.71% on 2026-09-03 and 6.76% on 2026-09-10 (https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-671, https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/30-year-mortgage-rate/news/582880). Guide and seasonal-fee comment: Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904). The fee inputs are macro proxies the company has not confirmed. Shares the Q2 release with the credit finding.

findings.finding: The quarter's rise in long yields should cut tangible book. All $885M of securities are available-for-sale (Q2 deck), and the 10-year went from 4.42% on 2026-06-30 to 5.11% on 2026-09-23 (a reported +85bp for the quarter). At an agency-MBS duration of ~4-6, that implies a pre-tax AOCI loss of roughly $30-45M, or about $1.2-1.8 of TBV per share against $25.46 at June 30, with TCE/TA falling from 7.49% toward ~7.0%. That reverses the Q2 deck's pitch that 'AOCI recovery supports TBV'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior WASH print in the baseline turned on AOCI/TBV alone. The 2022-23 TBV drawdown (TCE/TA to ~5.7% per the deck chart) coincided with the P/TBV multiple de-rating from ~210% to ~135%.
findings.why_not_priced: Every investor can see the rate move, but none of the published previews (Benzinga, Tickflow, Chartmill) quantify a TBV figure for this name. At ~1.45x TBV and a stock above the average target, a TBV decline lifts P/TBV to ~1.53x on the print. If it were priced, the stock would have de-rated toward peers' ~1.3x already; it is only -6% over 20 days.
findings.independence: Yield path: Morningstar/Dow Jones, 10-year at 4.420% on 2026-06-30 (https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202606307321/10-year-treasury-yield-rises-to-4420-data-talk), and 5.11% on 2026-09-23 (https://statisticsoftheworld.com/news/2026-09-23). The portfolio duration is my assumption, not a company number. This is a macro-to-company proxy and a below-the-line capital item, so it is sized as a fraction.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16. Washington Trust's own Q2 deck says 'the balance sheet is expected to benefit from rate increases' with 63% of loans variable-rate ($1.95B repricing within one month). That supports the 2.80% Q4 NIM guide and makes a held-or-raised NIM outlook on the call more likely than a cut. Against it: one-month funding repricing is $2.66B, and short funding (FHLB $456M) reprices with a 2-year yield that rose ~75bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 delivered NIM +10bp and a stated Q3/Q4 NIM path, and the stock rose +8.15% (with credit stabilizing). Chartmill noted an earlier Q2 beat that 'lacked forward outlook' and left the stock flat. The guide matters on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The market reads a rate hike as bad for regional banks through credit and AOCI, and WASH drifted -6% in 20 days alongside rising yields. The company's own disclosure that NII benefits from hikes is in a deck slide, not in any preview. If priced, the stock would have held up relative to the yield move.
findings.independence: Company repricing table and 'benefit from rate increases' statement, Q2 deck slide 6 (https://s202.q4cdn.com/917433312/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Investor-Presentation-Q2-2026.pdf). Peer read: Citizens' Q3 2026 NIM rose 2bp to 3.19% even as interest-bearing deposit costs rose 5bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000759944/000075994426000206/a3q26earningsrelease.htm); Regions' NIM rose to 3.68% (https://finviz.com/news/403470/regions-reports-earnings-of-611-million-and-eps-of-071-in-3q-2026).

findings.finding: Office credit is open, not resolved. At June 30, $28.9M of office loans were on nonaccrual: Class A $22.3M, which pushed past-dues from 0.33% to 0.81%, and lab space $6.6M. A further $3.75M Class B special-mention loan matured in Q3 with the company 'in discussion with the sponsor'. The ACL is 0.83% and Q2 net charge-offs were $55K, so a charge-off or foreclosure on the Class A loan, or migration of the Class B loan, would hit Q3. A payoff would be a positive. Nothing public dates either outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line the stock trades on. Q1 2026's two office loans moving to nonaccrual took it -16.9%. Q2's stable nonaccruals (0.78% vs 0.81%) and lower provision took it +8.15%.
findings.why_not_priced: Unknown in either direction. The office table is public and the outcome is not, so the stock carries the risk without a sign. No foreclosure notice, court filing or sale was found to settle it before the print.
findings.independence: Q2 call: Class B $3.8M maturing, sponsor talks (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904). Q1 coverage of the two office loans and specific reserves (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/wash-q1-deep-dive-office-222951754.html). Shares the Q2 deck with finding 2.

findings.why_not_priced: There is nothing to price: the money buys optionality, and the cadence matches the prior three shelves. The only risk would be an equity raise announced with results if TBV/TCE fell enough (see finding 2), and nothing suggests one.
